reading.body:
Global DC OY is a plausible small Finnish data-center business, not a confirmed one: its name carries the signal, and nothing else in the record does.

The evidence is a single OpenStreetMap tag, telecom=data_center, attached to a way in Finland at 60.6289, 25.2625, about 24 miles from Helsinki Vantaa Airport. The name resolves into a Finnish limited company suffix, OY, and a DC that plausibly stands for data center. That naming pattern is what real hosting and colocation firms use, which is why this record reads as more likely genuine than the other low-information European rows reviewed alongside it.

What the record does not contain is the part that matters for AI. There is no operator, no website, no stated capacity, and no power figure. The megawatt field is zero, which here means unrecorded rather than zero consumption. No Finnish business registration was confirmed, and the research note states that search quota ran out before any operator site or press coverage could be checked. So the facility's service offering, size, and current operating status are all unknown.

For a site about compute and the grid, this is a placeholder, not a data point. It establishes that a company with a data-center name exists at a set of coordinates near Helsinki. It says nothing about how much power it draws, whether it is running, or whether it is large enough to matter to any AI workload. The honest reading is that Finland has small colocation businesses that OpenStreetMap contributors know about and public sources have not yet documented.
